Early life and education After the deaths of their parents in 1870, James Naismith and his sister and brother were raised by their bachelor uncle Peter Johnston Young in a Scottish-immigrant environment on a farm north of Almonte, Ont. Educated at nearby Bennies Corners and Almonte’s high school, and after spending some time in a lumber camp, Jim enrolled in Montreal’s McGill College in 1882 on a scholarship, bent on the ministry.
